nodes.label: Event and score sources
nodes.summary: Search logs, views, game servers: streams of events or score updates.

nodes.label: Viewer or player
nodes.summary: Asks for the top K, or for their own rank.

nodes.label: Stream summarisers
nodes.summary: One per partition; events for the same item always reach the same one. Hold bounded counters per time bucket.

nodes.label: Space-Saving counters
nodes.summary: Monitors only m items; when an unmonitored item arrives it replaces the item with the smallest count and records the possible over-count. Counts are bounded estimates.

nodes.label: Time buckets
nodes.summary: One summary per minute (tumbling window); old buckets are dropped; the window answer merges the buckets in range.

nodes.label: Merge service
nodes.summary: Collects each partition's top candidates with counts and error bounds, sums per item, sorts, and produces the global top K per scope. Correct only if items are partitioned by key or enough candidates are collected.

nodes.label: Leaderboard store (sorted sets)
nodes.summary: Ordered sets of member and score: O(log N) update and rank in Redis sorted sets (documented). Sharding by score range or member hash at scale is our design, and scores should also be persisted in a database (not drawn).

nodes.label: Result cache
nodes.summary: Holds the current top K per scope with a short TTL so reads do not recompute.

nodes.label: Top-K API
nodes.summary: Serves top K and rank queries from the cache or the leaderboard store.

nodes.label: Alternative: Count-Min Sketch
nodes.summary: Another widely used approximate-frequency structure; its paper could not be retrieved, so nothing is claimed about it.

edges.label: top candidates with counts and error

flows.name: Trending items for the last hour

steps.caption: Each event goes to the summariser that owns its item.
The item's count is updated in the current minute's bucket, evicting the smallest counter if the table is full.
Periodically each partition reports its top candidates with counts and error bounds.
The merge service sums counts per item and stores the global top K.
The API serves it from the cache.
A score update is applied to the player's sorted set entry in O(log N).
The player asks for their rank.
The API asks the store for the rank (counting members above), and returns the top N plus the player's position.

flows.name: Merging per-shard lists that are split by event (failure mode)

steps.caption: Events for one item were spread across partitions, so its count in each partition is below every local cut-off.
The merge sees the item in no local list and omits it although its total is among the largest; fix by partitioning on item or collecting extra candidates (our design reasoning).
No report arrives from one partition.
The API keeps serving the cached result and marks it stale rather than showing a list that omits that partition's items (our design reasoning).
